title: SAM2 streaming object-memory Mirror code
hypothesis: For four prompted objects in one short video, two per-object Givens angles can reconstruct object-specific SAM2 memory features from one per-frame shared memory tensor with >=25% lower actual session-state bytes, at <=1pp J&F loss versus native per-object memory, and outperform a matched rank-1 additive memory code.
scope: Official SAM2.1 Hiera-tiny video predictor on one deterministic synthetic 5-frame CPU clip. This is not natural-video or benchmark evidence.

scene.occlusion: objects cross/partially overlap during deterministic motion

memory_target: per-object output_dict_per_obj[*][frame].maskmem_features; output masks, object pointers, scores, input mask prompts and metadata remain private and are charged unchanged.
mirror_coordinate: per object and memory frame m=(theta_1,theta_2), analytically fit two channel-pair Givens rotations (0,1) and (2,3) of a shared cross-object mean memory tensor; all other memory channels reconstruct from the common base.
training: none; codes are fitted causally from current-frame object memories after each frame output and before future frames are processed. No future frame or ground-truth mask is used to fit codes.

metrics.quality: per-object J, boundary F, mean J&F, identity assignment switches, off-diagonal cross-object mask IoU
metrics.storage: actual self-describing serialized session payload bytes, including SAM2 checkpoint/config, normalized video frame cache, all input prompts, prediction masks, object pointers/scores, memory reconstruction bases/codes and metadata
metrics.compute: full forward wall/FPS, encode/decode wall, Givens FLOP proxy vs additive MAC proxy

success_gate: Mirror full session payload >=25% below independent; mean J&F no more than 1pp below independent; no additional ID switches; and at least 1pp higher mean J&F than rank-1 additive at equal or fewer bytes.
failure_gate: Rank-1 additive matches/beats Mirror quality, or Mirror misses independent quality/ID-switch tolerance.
